title: Punica: Multi-Tenant LoRA Serving
problem: Serving multiple LoRA-fine-tuned model variants for different tenants requires inefficient memory and compute resources, as each tenant's adapted weights cannot easily share a single base model inference path without serialization overhead.
motivation: Multi-tenant serving enables efficient delivery of customized language models to many users while amortizing base model computation and memory costs across requests.
method: Punica combines requests from different customers' LoRA adapters (lightweight customizations of a base model) into larger processing batches that run together. It stores the LoRA weights in high-bandwidth memory (the fastest available memory tier), eliminating the overhead of shuffling data between slower storage. When certain adapter combinations can't run in the same batch, dynamic scheduling (real-time reordering) intelligently groups compatible requests together while maintaining high throughput.
key_novelty: Combining requests from different customers into shared processing batches lets them run the same base model computation together, even though each customer has different weight customizations, cutting per-request overhead.
contributions: System design for multi-tenant LoRA inference with request batching across different adapters
Memory hierarchy optimization to efficiently manage LoRA weight placement and access
Dynamic scheduling strategy to maximize GPU utilization while serving heterogeneous tenants
Demonstrated throughput improvements over per-adapter or serialized serving approaches
